system_overview: This is a model-checking configuration module that verifies an inductive invariant of the Prisoners specification. It checks that the conjunction of the type-correctness invariant and the counting invariant is preserved by every step of the next-state relation, confirming these properties are inductive. This is stronger than simply checking the invariant holds on reachable states -- it verifies that any state satisfying the invariant will continue to satisfy it after any valid transition.
actors_and_components: This module extends the parent Prisoners specification and defines an inductive invariant test specification. It reuses all actors and components from the parent module: the set of prisoners, the designated counter, the two switches, and the counting mechanism.
state_variables: All state variables are inherited from the parent Prisoners module: the two switch positions, the per-prisoner signal counts, and the counter's running tally.
initial_state: Instead of using the parent module's initial predicate, this module uses the combined type-correctness and counting invariant as the initial predicate. This means model checking starts from every state satisfying the invariant, not just the true initial states, which is how inductive invariant checking works.
actions: All actions are inherited from the parent Prisoners module. The next-state relation is the same: each step has exactly one prisoner enter the room and flip one switch according to the counting strategy.
safety_properties: The combined type-correctness and counting invariant must be preserved by every transition: if the system is in a state satisfying the invariant and takes a valid step, the resulting state must also satisfy the invariant. This establishes inductiveness.
model_bounds: Inherits the same constants as the parent specification: the set of prisoners and the designated counter must be instantiated with finite values for model checking.
additional_assumptions: The module notes that the number of states satisfying the type invariant is not much larger than the number of reachable states in the original specification, so TLC can verify the inductive invariant almost as quickly as it can check the original specification.
